**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-4086398, Reactome:R-HSA-2485179, Reactome:R-HSA-2514859)

#### 3. ectodermal dysplasia 17 with or without limb malformations  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.417)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-4086398)

**Proposed mechanism:** PDE6A (HGNC:8785) —DECREASES→ Canonical Wnt signaling pathway (GO:0060070); LEF1 (HGNC:6552) —DECREASES→ Canonical Wnt signaling pathway (GO:0060070); Canonical Wnt signaling pathway (GO:0060070) —LEADS_TO→ Retinitis pigmentosa (HP:0000510); Canonical Wnt signaling pathway (GO:0060070) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal dysplasia (HP:0000968). PDE6A and LEF1 converge on the modulation of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway. Loss of PDE6A function disrupts cyclic nucleotide regulation which modulates Wnt-dependent retinal progenitor cell maintenance, while LEF1 loss directly impairs Wnt-mediated transcriptional activation required for ectodermal appendage development.

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be refuted if biochemical assays show that PDE6A mutations have zero impact on Wnt-target gene expression in retinal pigment epithelium or if LEF1 mutations are shown to be strictly gain-of-function in ectodermal dysplasia models. _(variant: rs121908553)_

**Why it matters:** Identification of shared Wnt-dependent regulatory nodes suggests that small molecule Wnt-pathway modulators currently investigated for hair follicle regeneration might have utility in mitigating retinal degenerative processes related to PDE6A deficiency.
